physicalNotes: Radius 1.279 ± 0.037 ± 0.014 Jupiter radii (at 71492 km per Jupiter radius) from Mancini et al. 2018 (A&A 613, A41 (2018); arXiv:1802.03859): 91,438 km. No gravitational parameter is adopted. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: A straight line through six JWST transits of 2022 to 2026 measured in this project (src/objects/wasp-39b/source/science/jwst-transits/transit-times.csv; programmes 1366, 2783, 8017): 4.0552802 d, every transit within 0.2 min of it. Mancini et al. (2018, A&A 613, A41; arXiv:1802.03859) give 4.0552941 d, whose line runs 21 to 28 min late over these transits.
sources.shape: Inclination 87.32 degrees and a/R* = 11.07, DERIVED here from the paper’s fitted sum of fractional radii rA + rb = 0.10303 and ratio k = 0.14052 (a/R* = (1 + k)/(rA + rb)), not quoted. Eccentricity is set to 0: a circular display approximation, not an orbital solution.
sources.phase: The same line's transit nearest the scene epoch (2026-09-03): BMJD_TDB 61287.5104.
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
